sentences.en: This is a 99% Invisible Bonus episode.
sentences.zh: 这是一个《百分之九十九隐形》番外篇。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Recently, we published an episode called Towers of Silence.
sentences.zh: 最近，我们发布了一期名为《寂静之塔》的节目。

sentences.en: It's about how the Parsis in India are grappling with the loss of vultures
sentences.zh: 它讲述了印度的帕西人如何应对秃鹫的消失，

sentences.en: and how it changed something very intimate and meaningful for the community.
sentences.zh: 以及这如何改变了该社群非常私密且意义重大的一些习俗。

sentences.en: It was reported by our own Lash Madan, and it is epic, it is beautiful.
sentences.zh: 这期节目由我们自己的拉什·马丹报道，非常精彩，非常动人。

sentences.en: So first of all, go listen to that story if you haven't heard it.
sentences.zh: 所以首先，如果你还没听过那个故事，去听听吧。

sentences.en: It's so good.
sentences.zh: 真的太棒了。

sentences.en: It's so worth your time.
sentences.zh: 非常值得一听。

sentences.en: On the one hand, it's a very specific story.
sentences.zh: 一方面，这是一个非常独特的故事。

sentences.en: It's about a unique set of circumstances that happen to a very specific community.
sentences.zh: 它讲的是一个特定社群所经历的一系列独特境遇。

sentences.en: But it also feels universally relevant because it's a story about death
sentences.zh: 但它同时也具有普遍的现实意义，因为它是一个关于死亡的故事，

sentences.en: and how we choose to transition out of this world.
sentences.zh: 以及我们如何选择离开这个世界。

sentences.en: It's about how we might react when there's a major cultural shift that we cannot control.
sentences.zh: 它讲述了当我们遭遇无法控制的重大文化变迁时，我们可能会作何反应。

sentences.en: And importantly, it is about a keystone species collapse,
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，它关于一个关键物种的崩溃，

sentences.en: which is something that we are on track to see more of in these times.
sentences.zh: 而在当今这个时代，我们正注定会看到更多这样的情况。

sentences.en: And you, Lasha, collected a ton of information about vulture conservation in your reporting,
sentences.zh: 拉莎，你在报道中收集了大量关于秃鹫保护的信息，

sentences.en: and it didn't quite fit into the story that we wanted to tell.
sentences.zh: 它们并不能完全塞进我们想要讲述的故事里。

sentences.en: But it is so vital and so interesting that I wanted to have you on to talk more about that stuff specifically.
sentences.zh: 但这些内容太重要、太有趣了，所以我才请你来专门聊聊这些事。

sentences.en: So where we left off in the episode,
sentences.zh: 那么，接上期节目的结尾，

sentences.en: there's this hope that the vultures might one day return to the wild in huge numbers.
sentences.zh: 人们抱有一种希望，即秃鹫有朝一日能够大批重返大自然。

sentences.en: So I want to start there.
sentences.zh: 我想从这里开始聊起。

sentences.en: What is the deal with vultures in India, both in the wild and in captivity in present day 2024?
sentences.zh: 在当下的2024年，印度野生和人工圈养的秃鹫情况究竟如何？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Hi, Roman.
sentences.zh: 你好，罗曼。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: There's a lot in here, and there's, you know, a lot that didn't quite fit into the main episode
sentences.zh: 这里面内容很多，你知道的，有许多内容没能放进正片里，

sentences.en: that I'm excited to talk about.
sentences.zh: 对此我很兴奋能聊一聊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Specifically about all the other ways that humans relate to vultures
sentences.zh: 特别是关于人类与秃鹫产生联系的所有其他方式，

sentences.en: and all the kind of nerdy stuff about vulture conservation happening right now.
sentences.zh: 以及目前正在进行的、关于秃鹫保护的各种极客风的知识。

sentences.en: So there were three different species that experienced a dramatic decline between 95% to 99%.
sentences.zh: 当时有三个不同的物种经历了95%到99%的剧烈数量下降。

sentences.en: Today, there are eight vulture conservation and breeding centers in India,
sentences.zh: 如今，印度有八个秃鹫保护和繁育中心，

sentences.en: and there are a total of about 800 vultures in captivity.
sentences.zh: 圈养的秃鹫总数大约有800只。

sentences.en: It's estimated that throughout India, there were once about 40 million vultures in the wild.
sentences.zh: 据估计，整个印度的野外曾大约有4000万只秃鹫。

sentences.en: Today, that number is in the thousands.
sentences.zh: 而今天，这个数字只剩下几千只。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: And 800 vultures in captivity might sound like a small number,
sentences.zh: 圈养800只秃鹫听起来可能数字很小，

sentences.en: but it should be said that without vulture conservation,
sentences.zh: 但必须指出的是，如果没有秃鹫保护工作，

sentences.en: these vultures would have been completely extinct by now.
sentences.zh: 这些秃鹫现在已经彻底灭绝了。

sentences.en: So today, thanks to a number of factors, the banning of vulture toxic drugs,
sentences.zh: 所以今天，多亏了诸多因素——禁止对秃鹫有害的毒药、

sentences.en: public campaigns to use vulture safe drugs,
sentences.zh: 普及使用秃鹫安全药物的公众运动、

sentences.en: and all the work at these conservation centers to slowly and patiently breed healthy vultures,
sentences.zh: 以及这些保护中心为缓慢而耐心地繁育健康秃鹫所做的一切工作——

sentences.en: vulture populations in India are not declining.
sentences.zh: 印度的秃鹫数量没有在下降。

sentences.en: They're not facing extinction.
sentences.zh: 它们没有面临灭绝。

sentences.en: The populations across vulture species have stabilized,
sentences.zh: 各个秃鹫物种的种群数量已经稳定下来，

sentences.en: but we're not seeing a wholesale increase in the vulture population.
sentences.zh: 但我们并没有看到秃鹫种群数量的整体激增。

sentences.en: So it's not like we can say the work is over.
sentences.zh: 所以这并不是说我们可以宣布大功告成了。

sentences.en: And test releases of these captive vultures are happening.
sentences.zh: 这些人工圈养秃鹫的野外试放正在进行中。

sentences.en: But as we left off in the story, it's largely a waiting game
sentences.zh: 但正如我们在节目结尾所讲的那样，这在很大程度上是一场等待的游戏，

sentences.en: because vulture toxic drugs are still out there in the wild.
sentences.zh: 因为野外仍然存在对秃鹫有害的药物。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And so what is the process of vulture conservation?
sentences.zh: 那么秃鹫保护的过程是怎样的呢？

sentences.en: Like, what do they do?
sentences.zh: 比如说，他们都做些什么？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I was lucky enough to visit the largest vulture conservation and breeding center.
sentences.zh: 我有幸参观了最大的秃鹫保护和繁育中心。

sentences.en: It's in Panjore in a state of India called Haryana in North India.
sentences.zh: 它位于印度北部哈里亚纳邦的皮焦尔。

sentences.en: And it was opened in 2001 by Dr. Vibhu Prakash, who, if you listen to the episode,
sentences.zh: 它于2001年由维布·普拉卡什博士创立，如果你听过这期节目，

sentences.en: he is, he refutes the title that he's been given by many people as the vulture king of India.
sentences.zh: 就会知道他拒绝了许多人授予他的“印度秃鹫之王”的称号。

sentences.en: He doesn't like that.
sentences.zh: 他不喜欢这个称呼。

sentences.en: But he is considered the leading vulture biologiSt.
sentences.zh: 但他被认为是顶尖的秃鹫生物学家。

sentences.en: He happened to be doing research kind of begrudgingly on vultures.
sentences.zh: 他当时其实是带着些许勉强的心态在做秃鹫研究。

sentences.en: He wasn't so interested in vultures at the time.
sentences.zh: 在那时，他对秃鹫并没有那么感兴趣。

sentences.en: This is before the decline because he was more interested in species that were
sentences.zh: 这发生在数量骤减之前，因为他当时对那些

sentences.en: rare or harder to find.
sentences.zh: 稀有或更难找到的物种更感兴趣。

sentences.en: And vultures were kind of boring to him because they were just everywhere.
sentences.zh: 秃鹫对 lubricants（注：原文slip of tongue/audio anomaly caught as boring to him）他来说有点无趣，因为它们随处可见。

sentences.en: And then all of a sudden he became the person who
sentences.zh: 然后突然之间，他成了那个

sentences.en: happened to have so much knowledge because of the research he'd been doing.
sentences.zh: 恰好因之前一直在做研究而拥有渊博知识的人。

sentences.en: And so what did the conservation center actually look like?
sentences.zh: 那么保护中心实际上长什么样？

sentences.en: It didn't look quite like what I expected it to look like.
sentences.zh: 它看起来不太像我预期的那样。

sentences.en: It was a bunch of concrete warehouses, essentially.
sentences.zh: 从根本上说，它是一堆混凝土仓库。

sentences.en: To get there, I drove down or I was driven down a very windy road.
sentences.zh: 为了到达那里，我沿着一条非常弯曲的路开过来，或者说我被司机载着开过来。

sentences.en: We got lost so many times that we had to stop, pull over multiple times and ask people,
sentences.zh: 我们迷路了无数次，以至于不得不停下车，多次靠边向路人打听，

sentences.en: hey, do you know where the vulture conservation center is?
sentences.zh: 喂，你知道秃鹫保护中心在哪里吗？

sentences.en: Nobody knew what we were talking about.
sentences.zh: 没有人知道我们在说什么。

sentences.en: And there's also no signage, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，那里也没有任何标牌。

sentences.en: If you remember from the episode, vultures are easily freaked out by humans.
sentences.zh: 如果你还记得节目里的内容，秃鹫很容易被人类吓到。

sentences.en: Vultures will vomit as a response to being close to humans.
sentences.zh: 秃鹫在接近人类时会有呕吐的反应。

sentences.en: It can also interrupt their laying pattern.
sentences.zh: 这也会打断它们的产卵规律。

sentences.en: All to say that conservationists don't really want these centers to attract a ton of attention
sentences.zh: 总而言之，环保主义者其实并不希望这些中心吸引大量注意，

sentences.en: or for them to randomly get curious visitors.
sentences.zh: 也不希望它们随随便便引来好奇的游客。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: Which for me meant that it was hard to find.
sentences.zh: 对我而言，这意味着它很难找到。

sentences.en: But eventually I did get there and I was given a tour by Nikita Prakash.
sentences.zh: 但最终我还是到了那里，尼基塔·普拉卡什带我参观了基地。

sentences.en: Nikita currently runs the center.
sentences.zh: 尼基塔目前负责管理这个中心。

sentences.en: She also happens to be the wife of Vibhu Prakash.
sentences.zh: 她恰好也是维布·普拉卡什的妻子。

sentences.en: Together they've been involved in vulture research and conservation for decades.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，他们一直携手从事秃鹫的研究和保护工作。

sentences.en: Wow, it's very tall.
sentences.zh: 哇，它太高了。

sentences.en: These aviaries.
sentences.zh: 这些大型鸟舍。

sentences.en: 20 feet high, 40 feet wide, and 100 feet long.
sentences.zh: 高20英尺，宽40英尺，长100英尺。

sentences.en: I mentioned it was the largeSt.
sentences.zh: 我提过这是最大的一处。

sentences.en: So there's 800 vultures in captivity total throughout India.
sentences.zh: 全印度圈养的秃鹫总共有800只。

sentences.en: This center has 400 of them.
sentences.zh: 这个中心就养了400只。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: And, you know, there's a bunch of different rooMs.
sentences.zh: 而且，这里有许多不同的房间。

sentences.en: A breeding room.
sentences.zh: 育种室。

sentences.en: There's an incubation room.
sentences.zh: 还有一个孵化室。

sentences.en: This is our intubation and pruder room.
sentences.zh: 这是我们的孵化和育雏室。

sentences.en: Shall I show you from inside?
sentences.zh: 要我带你在里面看看吗？

sentences.en: There's a little warehouse-looking thing where they house the food for the vultures, which
sentences.zh: 这里有一个看起来像小仓库的地方，他们在那儿存放秃鹫的食物，

sentences.en: is all goat.
sentences.zh: 全部都是山羊肉。

sentences.en: So that is our food processing room.
sentences.zh: 所以那是我们的食品加工室。

sentences.en: When the goats are brought here, then we, according to the number of vultures, we prepare and we
sentences.zh: 当山羊被带到这里后，我们会根据秃鹫的数量进行准备，

sentences.en: provide the food.
sentences.zh: 然后提供食物。

sentences.en: And then there's just rows and rows of cement aviaries.
sentences.zh: 接着就是一排又一排的水泥鸟舍。

sentences.en: You can't really get a clear view of vultures except through these windows that are cut through
sentences.zh: 除了透过这些在水泥上凿出的窗户外，

sentences.en: the cement.
sentences.zh: 你很难看清秃鹫的全貌。

sentences.en: And inside, vultures sit on ledges and perches embedded into the walls.
sentences.zh: 在里面，秃鹫栖息在嵌入墙壁的岩架和栖木上。

sentences.en: And there's a roof made of strong metal mesh to make sure that no other animals, like leopards
sentences.zh: 屋顶由坚固的金属网制成，以确保豹子等其他动物

sentences.en: and whatnot, will get inside.
sentences.zh: 无法钻进来。

sentences.en: Every aviary has four baths that are cleaned twice a week.
sentences.zh: 每个鸟舍都有四个每周清洗两次的水池。

sentences.en: Also twice a week, the vultures are fed.
sentences.zh: 同样是每周两次，秃鹫会被喂食。

sentences.en: And they're fed through a little door where skinned goat carcasses are just slid through.
sentences.zh: 食物是通过一个小门送进去的，去皮的山羊尸体就从那里滑进去。

sentences.en: Wow, this feels like a lot of effort to maintain.
sentences.zh: 哇，感觉维护工作需要付出巨大的努力。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, the two of them are so committed.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们俩太投入了。

sentences.en: They're so committed to this work.
sentences.zh: 他们对这项工作投入了极大的心血。

sentences.en: Nikita told me that the religion she practices is called Jainism.
sentences.zh: 尼基塔告诉我，她信仰的宗教叫耆那教。

sentences.en: And in Jainism, you don't eat meat.
sentences.zh: 在耆那教中，你不吃肉。

sentences.en: But in addition to meat, you also don't eat anything that grows underground.
sentences.zh: 但除了肉类，你也不能吃任何在地下生长的东西。

sentences.en: So garlic, eggs, onions, or eggs don't grow underground.
sentences.zh: 所以大蒜、洋葱，嗯，鸡蛋不是长在地下的。

sentences.en: So garlic, onions, you know.
sentences.zh: 所以大蒜、洋葱，你懂的。

sentences.en: And yet, she watches 400 vultures eat skinned goat meat twice a week with an extreme dedication.
sentences.zh: 然而，她却带着极大的奉献精神，看着400只秃鹫每周吃两次剥皮的山羊肉。

sentences.en: And yet you watch the vultures consume...
sentences.zh: 然而你看着秃鹫吞食……

sentences.en: I eat nestlings on goat meat.
sentences.zh: 我吃山羊肉里的小雏鸟（注：此处原文口误/发音粘连，顺译）。

sentences.en: And you say that with a big smile.
sentences.zh: 而你脸上带着灿烂的笑容说出这话。

sentences.en: Now I'm used to it.
sentences.zh: 现在我习惯了。

sentences.en: It's very interesting.
sentences.zh: 这非常有趣。

sentences.en: So there's one other room at the conservation center.
sentences.zh: 保护中心里还有另一个房间。

sentences.en: It's a pretty simple room.
sentences.zh: 那是一个相当简单的房间。

sentences.en: The biggest thing, the most obvious thing that's in there is a large monitor that has a series of CCTV cameras on them.
sentences.zh: 里面最显眼、最明显的东西是一个大显示屏，上面连接着一系列闭路电视摄像头。

sentences.en: It's a control room, essentially.
sentences.zh: 从本质上讲，这是一个控制室。

sentences.en: And Vibhu and Nikita and a lot of their staff spent a lot of time in there.
sentences.zh: 维布、尼基塔以及他们的许多员工都在那里度过了大量时间。

sentences.en: And this is how they observe vulture behavior.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们观察秃鹫行为的方式。

sentences.en: I learned that sometimes Vibhu would even sleep in the room and occasionally watch the CCTV screen just to make sure that the vultures are doing okay.
sentences.zh: 我了解到，有时维布甚至会睡在房间里，时不时盯着闭路电视屏幕，只为了确保秃鹫安然无恙。

sentences.en: Every time an egg is to hatch, he sleeps here to make sure that it hatches.
sentences.zh: 每当有蛋要孵化时，他就睡在这里以确保顺利破壳。

sentences.en: Do you have children?
sentences.zh: 你们有孩子吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, we have two boys.
sentences.zh: 对，我们有两个男孩。

sentences.en: All these 400 vultures are kind of like your wild children.
sentences.zh: 这所有的400只秃鹫就像是你们野外的孩子一样。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I took care of newborn twins.
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，我曾照顾过刚出生的双胞胎。

sentences.en: It sounds exactly the same.
sentences.zh: 听起来完全是一回事。

sentences.en: You're just like always making sure they're alive.
sentences.zh: 你就是得时刻确保它们还活着。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I mean, the one major difference, I guess, is in their case, the whole future of a species is kind of riding on their dedication.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，最大的不同在于，在它们（秃鹫）的案例中，整个物种的未来都系于他们的奉献之上。

sentences.en: So it's, yeah, it's a lot.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，压力很大。

sentences.en: And during the height of COVID in India, everything was highly militarized and locked down.
sentences.zh: 在印度新冠疫情最严重的时候，一切都高度军事化并处于封锁状态。

sentences.en: And so Vibhu and Nikita and their staff really struggled to get to the conservation center because to be able to travel, you needed to move through various checkpoints.
sentences.zh: 因此，维布、尼基塔和他们的员工很难到达保护中心，因为要想出行，你必须穿过各种检查站。

sentences.en: But then they also really struggled to find enough meat, to find enough food for the vultures to survive.
sentences.zh: 但同时，他们也很难找到足够的肉类，找到足够让秃鹫生存的食物。

sentences.en: And they were really worried.
sentences.zh: 他们当时非常担心。

sentences.en: They told me they worked until they wilted.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉我，他们工作到筋疲力尽。

sentences.en: During corona, we were not worried for ourselves.
sentences.zh: 在新冠疫情期间，我们并没有为自己担心。

sentences.en: We were worried about the vultures, how food will come for them.
sentences.zh: 我们担心的是秃鹫，它们的食物该怎么解决。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, we would get nightmare, how to get food.
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，我们常常会做噩梦，发愁怎么弄到食物。

sentences.en: And we were contemplating releasing them because we were, one week we could not get food.
sentences.zh: 而且我们甚至考虑过放飞它们，因为有整整一周我们都找不到食物。

sentences.en: But release them, then what will happen?
sentences.zh: 但如果放飞了，接下来会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: So in spite of all the barriers and restrictions, we would come to the center every day.
sentences.zh: 所以尽管有重重阻碍和限制，我们每天还是会来到救助中心。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Every day.
sentences.zh: 每天都来。

sentences.en: And then mobilize the forest department because they can, they have access, they can give you permission to get food.
sentences.zh: 然后去动员林业部门，因为他们有权限，可以批准你们获取食物。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And you did it.
sentences.zh: 而你们做到了。

sentences.en: We did it.
sentences.zh: 我们做到了。

sentences.en: You were able to feed the vultures every week.
sentences.zh: 你们每周都能喂养秃鹫。

sentences.en: Every week.
sentences.zh: 每周。

sentences.en: So is there a lot of support for the work?
sentences.zh: 那么这项工作得到了很多支持吗？

sentences.en: Like, do other people recognize how important this is?
sentences.zh: 比如说，其他人意识到这有多重要了吗？

sentences.en: As you can probably imagine, vultures are not a sexy animal.
sentences.zh: 正如你大概能想象的那样，秃鹫可不是什么迷人的动物。

sentences.en: You know, they don't compare to the amount of attention and money that tiger conservation gets, for example.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它们根本无法和老虎保护项目获得的关注度和资金相提并论。

sentences.en: And vulture conservation also has to contend with not only public apathy, but active fear.
sentences.zh: 而且秃鹫保护工作不仅要面对公众的冷漠，还要面对切实的恐惧。

sentences.en: A lot of people fear vultures.
sentences.zh: 很多人都害怕秃鹫。

sentences.en: I spoke to one vulture biologist who told me about a time he was doing research and trapping vultures in a particular village in India.
sentences.zh: 我曾跟一位秃鹫生物学家聊过，他告诉我当年他在印度某村庄做研究、捕捉秃鹫的经历。

sentences.en: And he learned that in this area, vultures were such a bad omen that if they were seen to be landing on someone's house,
sentences.zh: 他了解到，在这个地方，秃鹫被视为极大的不祥之兆，如果看到它们落在谁家的房顶上，

sentences.en: it was thought that what that meant is that someone in that house is going to die.
sentences.zh: 人们就会认为这意味着那家里会有人去世。

sentences.en: And so what they would do is dismantle that house, move out and build a new home.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会把那栋房子拆了，搬走，然后盖一栋新房子。

sentences.en: It's hard to get people who have money, including governments, to see how important vultures are as a keystone species, that their conservation is really important.
sentences.zh: 很难让有钱人，包括政府，去认识到秃鹫作为基石物种有多重要，认识到保护它们至关重要。

sentences.en: It's also really expensive because for each goat to go through the testing to make sure that what's in the goat system will not kill the vultures, that's really expensive.
sentences.zh: 而且成本也非常高，因为每只山羊都要经过检测，以确保其体内的成分不会毒死秃鹫，这真的花销巨大。

sentences.en: And so vulture conservation is contending with just the need for a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 因此，秃鹫保护工作不得不面对资金严重短缺的问题。

sentences.en: Yeah, so we know that the vultures have always meant a great deal to the Parsis in India.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们知道秃鹫对印度的帕西人来说一直有着极其重大的意义。

sentences.en: But what other changes has the vultures' absence brought about to India as a whole?
sentences.zh: 但秃鹫的消失给整个印度带来了哪些其他变化呢？

sentences.en: It's changed, you know, the vultures created this void.
sentences.zh: 情况变了，你知道的，秃鹫的消失留下了这样一个真空地带。

sentences.en: Vultures are a keystone species, which means if this species disappears or dramatically reduces in size, it shifts everything.
sentences.zh: 秃鹫是一个基石物种，这意味着如果这个物种消失或数量急剧减少，整个生态系统都会发生巨变。

sentences.en: So, when vultures were around, there was this very specific cycle that existed in India whenever a cow carcass or any other kind of animal carcass would die.
sentences.zh: 所以，当秃鹫还在的时候，印度存在着一个非常特定的循环，每当有牛或其他动物的尸体死亡时就会启动。

sentences.en: The carcasses of animals used to just be left all over the countryside.
sentences.zh: 动物的尸体过去往往就被随手丢弃在乡村各处。

sentences.en: A cow dies in the field, they'd just leave it and the vultures would come.
sentences.zh: 一头牛死在田里，他们就留在那儿，秃鹫就会赶来。

sentences.en: Very convenient, very handy.
sentences.zh: 非常方便，非常省事。

sentences.en: Didn't have to touch it, didn't have to move it.
sentences.zh: 不需要去碰它，也不需要去挪动它。

sentences.en: Most of these cows are left to die naturally, and vultures were always the reliable cleanup crew.
sentences.zh: 这些牛大多是自然死亡的，而秃鹫一直都是可靠的清理大队。

sentences.en: So, a cow would die.
sentences.zh: 所以，一头牛死后。

sentences.en: Then a group of people in India known as cattle skinners would come, and they would skin the cow.
sentences.zh: 印度一群被称为剥皮匠的人就会赶来，把牛皮剥掉。

sentences.en: Often they'd be on call.
sentences.zh: 他们通常是随叫随到的。

sentences.en: These skinners would show up with a crew.
sentences.zh: 这些剥皮匠会带着一个团队出现。

sentences.en: Sometimes the skinners would find work by just looking at the sky and seeing where, looking at the general area that vultures were beginning to circle.
sentences.zh: 有时，剥皮匠会通过观察天空、看哪个大致区域有秃鹫开始盘旋来寻找工作。

sentences.en: That makes sense.
sentences.zh: 这倒也合理。

sentences.en: This work is hard.
sentences.zh: 这项工作很辛苦。

sentences.en: And often it's this kind of work that you inherit through the caste system.
sentences.zh: 而且往往这种工作是通过种姓制度世袭的。

sentences.en: Often this work is designated to people who are lower caste.
sentences.zh: 这种工作通常是由低种姓的人来承担。

sentences.en: And this is how they make their living.
sentences.zh: 这也是他们谋生的手段。

sentences.en: They sell the hide to the leather industry.
sentences.zh: 他们把皮革卖给制革工业。

sentences.en: But this process also, interestingly, helps the vultures.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，这个过程对秃鹫也有所帮助。

sentences.en: The vultures don't need their food to be skinned.
sentences.zh: 秃鹫不需要别人帮它们的食物剥皮。

sentences.en: But once it's skinned, it makes it easier for vultures to access the meat.
sentences.zh: 但一旦剥了皮，秃鹫吃肉就更容易了。

sentences.en: Because vulture beaks actually can't penetrate cattle skin.
sentences.zh: 因为秃鹫的喙其实无法刺破牛皮。

sentences.en: It's too tough.
sentences.zh: 牛皮太坚韧了。

sentences.en: And so they access the innards only through, like, the eyes and the mouth and such.
sentences.zh: 所以它们只能通过眼睛、嘴巴之类的部位去吃内脏。

sentences.en: And so it's just, it's a little bit messier.
sentences.zh: 所以这就有点麻烦。

sentences.en: It takes more time.
sentences.zh: 需要花更多的时间。

sentences.en: So it's not like a necessity, but it's, you know, it helps them out a little bit.
sentences.zh: 因此这算不上必需，但你知道的，确实能给它们帮点小忙。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Makes sense.
sentences.zh: 有道理。

sentences.en: And so, okay, so the cow dies, the skinners come, and now the vultures are here.
sentences.zh: 所以，好吧，牛死了，剥皮匠来了，现在秃鹫也来了。

sentences.en: Once the vultures do their job, a separate group of workers called bone collectors come.
sentences.zh: 等秃鹫完成工作后，另一拨被称为捡骨工的工人就会出现。

sentences.en: And they collect the bones that are left.
sentences.zh: 他们会收集剩下的骨头。

sentences.en: And they sell these bones.
sentences.zh: 然后把这些骨头卖掉。

sentences.en: And that's how they make their money.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们赚钱的方式。

sentences.en: And these bones are mostly sold to fertilizer companies.
sentences.zh: 这些骨头大多卖给了化肥公司。

sentences.en: So it's this whole economic cycle all around the natural death of a cow.
sentences.zh: 所以，围绕着一头牛的自然死亡，形成了这样一个完整的经济循环。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So when the vultures stopped coming, this cycle broke.
sentences.zh: 所以当秃鹫不再出现时，这个循环就打破了。

sentences.en: And there was an attempt to implement a system called carcass dump sites.
sentences.zh: 人们曾试图推行一种名为尸体倾倒场的系统。

sentences.en: Essentially, carcass landfills on the outskirts of towns and villages.
sentences.zh: 本质上就是城镇和村庄郊区的尸体垃圾填埋场。

sentences.en: And when the vultures stopped coming, most towns and villages started creating these carcass dumps.
sentences.zh: 当秃鹫不再光顾时，大多数城镇和村庄开始建立这些尸体倾倒场。

sentences.en: Like they collect, new jobs came up, they collect the carcasses, they dump them in this one area.
sentences.zh: 就像他们收集那样，催生了新的工作岗位，他们收集尸体，然后把它们倾倒在同一个地方。

sentences.en: But these carcass dump sites led to a new problem.
sentences.zh: 但这些尸体倾倒场引发了一个新问题。

sentences.en: Now, when animals die, livestock dies, they're taken to these carcass dump sites where piles of cows and buffaloes and, you know, livestock are there.
sentences.zh: 现在，当动物死亡、牲畜死亡时，它们被运到这些尸体倾倒场，那里堆满了牛、水牛以及各种牲畜的尸体。

sentences.en: And so who is this?
sentences.zh: 那么这位是谁呢？

sentences.en: This is Munir Varani.
sentences.zh: 这位是穆尼尔·瓦拉尼。

sentences.en: He is a raptor biologist who worked alongside Vubu Prakash and dozens of other scientists back in the early 2000s to conclude that diclofenac was the thing that killed the vultures.
sentences.zh: 他是一名猛禽生物学家，曾在21世纪初与武布·普拉卡什以及数十位科学家并肩作战，最终得出结论：双氯芬酸钠是导致秃鹫死亡的元凶。

sentences.en: I remember that you would not see vultures at these carcass dump sites and you would see thousands of feral dogs.
sentences.zh: 我记得在这些尸体倾倒场你根本看不到秃鹫，却能看到成千上万只野狗。

sentences.en: They looked vicious.
sentences.zh: 它们看起来很凶残。

sentences.en: I mean, it was a scary thing.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那场面挺吓人的。

sentences.en: So Munir told me that these dump sites essentially became a breeding ground for feral dogs.
sentences.zh: 所以穆尼尔告诉我，这些倾倒场基本上成了野狗的滋生地。

sentences.en: Dogs started to breed even inside the rib cages of these cow carcasses.
sentences.zh: 狗甚至开始在这些牛尸的肋骨内繁殖。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Lasha.
sentences.zh: 拉莎。

sentences.en: Roman, I have photos and I could share them with you.
sentences.zh: 罗曼，我有照片，我可以分享给你。

sentences.en: Okay, okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧，好吧。

sentences.en: But I feel like I almost don't need to.
sentences.zh: 但我感觉我几乎不需要看。

sentences.en: You can imagine.
sentences.zh: 你能想象得到。

sentences.en: No, I got it.
sentences.zh: 不，我懂的。

sentences.en: So it was actually found that the population of feral dogs across India increased by 5.5 million in the same time period that the vulture population was rapidly declining in the in the 1990s and early 2000s.
sentences.zh: 结果人们发现，在20世纪90年代和21世纪初秃鹫种群急剧下降的同一时期，全印度的野狗数量增加了550万只。

sentences.en: And Roman, I don't know if you know this, but vultures only ever go after dead things.
sentences.zh: 罗曼，我不知道你知不知道这一点，但秃鹫只吃死物。

sentences.en: They never attack the living.
sentences.zh: 它们从不攻击活物。

sentences.en: Yeah, but I imagine dogs do.
sentences.zh: 对，但我想狗会。

sentences.en: Dogs do.
sentences.zh: 狗会的。

sentences.en: They actually they prey on the living.
sentences.zh: 它们实际上是以活物为食的。

sentences.en: Dogs also transmit rabies.
sentences.zh: 狗还会传播狂犬病。

sentences.en: And in India, rabies is a real concern.
sentences.zh: 在印度，狂犬病是个真正令人担忧的问题。

sentences.en: It's been a real concern for a long time.
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间以来它一直是个严峻的问题。

sentences.en: India has the highest number of rabies related deaths in the world.
sentences.zh: 印度的狂犬病相关死亡人数居世界之首。

sentences.en: There's a very strong correlation between the decline in vultures and the number of cases of rabies that have gone up.
sentences.zh: 秃鹫数量的减少与狂犬病病例的上升之间存在着非常强的相关性。

sentences.en: I mean, dog numbers have just skyrocketed because there's a super abundance of food now that is available that vultures used to get rid of in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 我是说，由于现在有超级丰盛的食物，而这些食物过去是由秃鹫来处理掉的，导致狗的数量急剧飙升。

sentences.en: And I imagine that the dogs are not these efficient, clean eaters the way the vultures are, right?
sentences.zh: 我想狗可不像秃鹫那样是高效、干净的食客，对吧？

sentences.en: They really just make a mess.
sentences.zh: 它们真的只会弄得一团糟。

sentences.en: My dog makes an incredible mess.
sentences.zh: 我的狗就把家里弄得一团糟。

sentences.en: You're right.
sentences.zh: 你说得对。

sentences.en: Unlike vultures, dogs, really anything else that would that would go for the carcass.
sentences.zh: 与秃鹫不同，狗或者其他任何会去啃食尸体的动物。

sentences.en: So dogs, rats, other birds of prey, like we mentioned in the episode, kites and crows.
sentences.zh: 所以像狗、老鼠、其他猛禽，就像我们在节目中提到的，鸢和乌鸦。

sentences.en: None of these animals are able to consume a carcass entirely.
sentences.zh: 这些动物没有一个能够把一具尸体完全吃光。

sentences.en: They're picky.
sentences.zh: 它们很挑剔。

sentences.en: And so what this means is two things happen environmentally.
sentences.zh: 所以这意味着在环境层面上会发生两件事。

sentences.en: The first is that these dogs, they are more likely to transmit the diseases that the vultures have historically prevented from spreading.
sentences.zh: 首先是这些狗更有可能传播那些以往被秃鹫阻止扩散的疾病。

sentences.en: Remember that the vultures' stomach is actually more acidic than battery acid.
sentences.zh: 记住，秃鹫的胃酸比蓄电池里的酸还要强。

sentences.en: Whoa.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: It can consume all the gnarly stuff and just kill it.
sentences.zh: 它能吞下所有奇奇怪怪的东西并直接将其消化杀死。

sentences.en: It can kill it inside its body, right?
sentences.zh: 它能在体内将其杀死，对吧？

sentences.en: But these dogs, they just pass on these diseases.
sentences.zh: 但这些狗只会把这些疾病传播下去。

sentences.en: And so it leads to potentially higher rates of infection.
sentences.zh: 因此这可能导致更高的感染率。

sentences.en: And the second thing, the second kind of big environmental consequence is that because there's no other animal that consumes an entire carcass,
sentences.zh: 第二件事，第二种重大环境后果是，由于没有其他动物能吃光整具尸体，

sentences.en: there's this risk that the dead carcass matter, whatever is in it, a disease or whatever, it can spread into the water and the soil.
sentences.zh: 这就存在一种风险，即死尸残渣中的物质——无论是疾病还是别的什么——会扩散到水体和土壤中。

sentences.en: It can leach into the water and the soil because the remains are not totally gone.
sentences.zh: 它们会渗入水和土壤中，因为残骸并没有完全消失。

sentences.en: And so it's a whole mess.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一团糟。

sentences.en: I mean, this is what you mean by a keystone species.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是你所说的基石物种的含义。

sentences.en: I mean, just like the whole system collapses.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，整个系统都崩溃了。

sentences.en: And the thing is that it's not something that is so visible to the human eye right away.
sentences.zh: 关键在于，这不是那种能立刻被人类肉眼察觉的事情。

sentences.en: You know, the thing that I found so compelling about the Parsi experience when it comes to vultures is that it's so tangible.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，关于帕西人与秃鹫的经历，最让我折服的是它是如此切实可感。

sentences.en: And sometimes, you know, in order for humans to care and to really see a change, it needs to be really in your face.
sentences.zh: 有时，你知道的，为了让人们在意并真正看到变化，必须得把问题直接摆在眼前。

sentences.en: And I think that's what made it so compelling.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是它如此引人注目的原因。

sentences.en: But all of this stuff is also happening in the background.
sentences.zh: 但所有这些事情同时也在幕后发生着。

sentences.en: That's a little bit harder to see that we should also care about.
sentences.zh: 那稍微有点难以察觉，但我们也应该同样去关注。

sentences.en: Recently,
sentences.zh: 最近，

sentences.en: there were two environmental economists who published this big body of work looking at vultures in India and the environmental consequences and economic consequences of vultures in India.
sentences.zh: 有两位环境经济学家发表了一项宏大的研究成果，考察了印度的秃鹫以及秃鹫在印度引发的环境后果和经济后果。

sentences.en: They found that on average, human death rates supposedly increased by more than 4% in what they call vulture-suitable districts after these birds nearly went extinct.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，在他们所称的适宜秃鹫生存的地区，在该鸟类近乎灭绝之后，人类的平均死亡率据称上升了4%以上。

sentences.en: So what they mean is that in the areas that they surveyed where vultures used to exist in high numbers and are now no longer there,
sentences.zh: 所以他们的意思是，在他们调查的那些曾经拥有大量秃鹫如今却已不复存在的地区，

sentences.en: the general mortality rate has seemed to increase by 4%.
sentences.zh: 总死亡率似乎上升了4%。

sentences.en: A large portion of this is attributed to rabies, but it could be, you know, all sorts of reasons for mortality.
sentences.zh: 其中很大一部分归因于狂犬病，但也可能是各种各样的死亡原因。

sentences.en: And they also found evidence that there's been an increase in feral dog populations and rabies and lower water quality in these regions.
sentences.zh: 他们还发现证据表明，这些地区的野狗数量和狂犬病有所增加，水质有所下降。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Okay, so it's clear that these vultures have left a void when it comes to waste management in India.
sentences.zh: 好吧，很显然，在印度的废物管理方面，秃鹫的消失留下了一个真空地带。

sentences.en: And they operated as this kind of immune system for the country.
sentences.zh: 它们起到了这个国家某种免疫系统的作用。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so what do you do now?
sentences.zh: 那么现在该怎么办呢？

sentences.en: How do you fill this void?
sentences.zh: 你该如何填补这个真空？

sentences.en: Because clearly the dogs aren't doing it and the carcass dumps aren't doing it.
sentences.zh: 因为很显然狗没有做到，尸体倾倒场也没有做到。

sentences.en: Like, what do you do?
sentences.zh: 就像，你该怎么做？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's almost making it—I mean, it's making it worse.
sentences.zh: 对，这简直是在让情况——我是说，这让情况变得更糟了。

sentences.en: It's making it worse.
sentences.zh: 这让情况变得更糟了。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a really—it's a really tough and interesting problem.
sentences.zh: 是的，这真的是一个——一个非常棘手且有趣的问题。

sentences.en: So what I found is that municipal governments all over India, not all, but some,
sentences.zh: 所以我发现，印度各地的市政府，不是全部，但有一部分

sentences.en: have been trying to figure out how to implement sustainable infrastructure to do the job that vultures did for millennia when it comes to waste management and sanitation services that the vultures provided.
sentences.zh: 一直试图弄清楚如何建立可持续的基础设施，来做秃鹰几千年来一直在做的工作，也就是秃鹰曾经提供的废物管理和卫生服务。

sentences.en: And so there are municipalities that are grappling with questions like, do we incinerate cows to prevent disease from spreading?
sentences.zh: 因此，有些市镇正在努力解决这样的问题：我们是否要焚烧牛只来防止疾病传播？

sentences.en: If we do, what are the kind of infrastructural hoops we need to go through to, like, one, make sure that people will do this once we build it?
sentences.zh: 如果我们这样做，我们需要经历什么样的基础设施考验，比如第一，确保我们建好后人们真的会这么做？

sentences.en: Or should we bury them?
sentences.zh: 还是应该把它们埋了？

sentences.en: Should we make carcass dump sites the official solution and somehow try to prevent dogs from getting in or something?
sentences.zh: 我们是否应该将动物尸体倾倒场作为官方解决方案，并想方设法阻止狗闯入或其他什么办法？

sentences.en: So different places in India are trying different possibilities.
sentences.zh: 因此，印度的不同地方正在尝试各种可能的方法。

sentences.en: But each idea comes with its own set of hurdles.
sentences.zh: 但每个想法都有其独特的一系列阻碍。

sentences.en: Burial and incineration cost money.
sentences.zh: 土葬和火葬都需要花钱。

sentences.en: And if the burden is on the farmer or the cattle owner to pay for disposing of its dead cattle, when prior to this ecological shift they had to do absolutely nothing,
sentences.zh: 如果处理死牛的经济负担要由农民或牛主人来承担，而在此次生态转变之前，他们根本不需要做任何事情，

sentences.en: are they going to?
sentences.zh: 他们会愿意承担吗？

sentences.en: Munir actually told me that some people just dump their dead animals into the Ganga because it's the cheapest option.
sentences.zh: 穆尼尔实际上告诉我，有些人只是把死去的动物直接扔进恒河，因为这是最便宜的选择。

sentences.en: And so you've got these bloated carcasses now just floating down the river.
sentences.zh: 所以你会看到这些发胀的尸体就这样顺流而下。

sentences.en: Oh, dear God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: That's an awful image of a bloated cow carcass floating down the river.
sentences.zh: 一头肿胀的牛尸顺流而下的画面太可怕了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And what we're seeing, too, is that as India's governments grapple with creating and implementing a new system of infrastructure, these systems will very likely,
sentences.zh: 我们还看到，随着印度各级政府努力建立和实施一套新的基础设施系统，这些系统极有可能，

sentences.en: and in some places already have, put the jobs of those cattle skinners and bone collectors at risk.
sentences.zh: 而且在某些地方已经让那些剥牛皮工和收骨工的工作面临风险。

sentences.en: Because if cows are being shipped off to an incineration center, they don't need to be skinned anymore.
sentences.zh: 因为如果牛被运送到焚烧中心，它们就不再需要被剥皮了。

sentences.en: So is there any hope to take these 800 vultures that are in captivity and release them and begin to solve some of these problems, at least in a small way?
sentences.zh: 那么，把这 800 只被圈养的秃鹰放归并开始解决其中一些问题，哪怕是以一种微小的方式，还有希望吗？

sentences.en: It's a really thin line between wanting to release these vultures and not wanting to send them off to their death.
sentences.zh: 在想要放归这些秃鹰和不想把它们送上绝路之间，有一条非常微妙的界限。

sentences.en: As mentioned in the main episode, these drugs, these toxic drugs are still out there and they're increasing in number.
sentences.zh: 正如主集里提到的，这些药物，这些有毒药物仍然存在，而且数量还在增加。

sentences.en: And some of them are slowly getting banned.
sentences.zh: 其中一些药物正在慢慢被禁。

sentences.en: Two of these newer toxic drugs were banned in 2023.
sentences.zh: 其中两种较新的有毒药物在 2023 年被禁。

sentences.en: But again, we also learned that banning a drug doesn't necessarily equal to the eradication of the drug in the environment.
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，我们也了解到，禁止某种药物并不一定等于彻底根除环境中的这种药物。

sentences.en: And so, yeah, and this is the thing that biologists who are behind this conservation work are really, really grappling with.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这也是支持这项保护工作的生物学家们真正、真正头疼的问题。

sentences.en: Because they can't control the drugs in the wider populace at all.
sentences.zh: 因为他们根本无法控制广大民众对这些药物的使用。

sentences.en: Yeah, so the main vulture conservation center, the one I visited, it's formally called the Jatayu Conservation and Breeding Center in Pinjor.
sentences.zh: 是的，主要的秃鹰保护中心，也就是我参观的那家，官方名称是位于平乔尔的贾塔尤保护与繁育中心。

sentences.en: And that name, Jatayu, it references a particular Hindu myth about a vulture god named Jatayu.
sentences.zh: 这个名字“贾塔尤”指的是一个关于秃鹰神贾塔尤的印度教神话。

sentences.en: In Hindu mythology, there's a vulture king, and he sacrifices his life to save a suffering human.
sentences.zh: 在印度教神话中，有一位秃鹰王，他牺牲了自己的生命来拯救一个受苦的人。

sentences.en: He was thought to have lived for over 6,000 years.
sentences.zh: 人们认为他活了 6000 多岁。

sentences.en: This vulture king was known for his kind heart and his strong wings.
sentences.zh: 这位秃鹰王以善良的心肠和强壮的翅膀而闻名。

sentences.en: And one day, he tries to save a human life.
sentences.zh: 有一天，他试图挽救一条人类的生命。

sentences.en: But in return, he was wounded, his wings were cut, and he was left to die in abject pain.
sentences.zh: 但作为回报，他受伤了，翅膀被砍断，并在极度痛苦中等死。

sentences.en: Oh, I mean, that is interesting that they chose that as a name because, you know, that's the story of a vulture ultimately dying.
sentences.zh: 哦，我的意思是，他们选择这个名字挺有意思的，因为你知道，那是一个秃鹰最终死去的故事情节。

sentences.en: But it's also this reminder of the fate that they're trying to avoid.
sentences.zh: 但这也是对它们正极力避免的那种命运的一种提醒。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think one thing I found kind of clever is that they use this myth about Jatayu in their public messaging.
sentences.zh: 是的，我觉得我发现的一个比较巧妙的地方是，他们在向公众宣传时运用了关于贾塔尤的神话。

sentences.en: So they go often from village to village and talk to people and try and get people to care about vultures.
sentences.zh: 所以他们经常挨家挨户地走访村庄，与人们交谈，试图让人们关心秃鹰。

sentences.en: Referencing this story, which is for a lot of people in India, it's like one of their main kind of reference points for vultures.
sentences.zh: 引用这个故事，对于印度的许多人来说，这是他们了解秃鹰的主要参考点之一。

sentences.en: It's kind of the one positive one, you know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 这可以说是唯一一个比较积极的切入点，你懂我的意思吧？

sentences.en: So Vibu told me that they're constantly working to persuade farmers to not use black market diclofenac or other toxic drugs.
sentences.zh: 所以维布告诉我，他们一直在说服农民不要使用黑市上的双氯芬酸或其他有毒药物。

sentences.en: Vibu's team collects carcass samples and they do routine drug tests.
sentences.zh: 维布的团队收集动物尸体样本并进行常规药物检测。

sentences.en: They find safe alternatives and they lobby the government and pharmaceutical companies to sell those instead.
sentences.zh: 他们寻找安全的替代品，并游说政府和制药公司转而销售这些替代品。

sentences.en: They also go undercover in drugstores pretending to be, you know, a farmer with a sick cow and and they they'll see if doctors still prescribe all these toxic drugs.
sentences.zh: 他们还私下暗访药店，假装自己是，你知道的，一个带着病牛的农民，然后他们会看看医生是否还在开这些有毒药物。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's it's really hands on work.
sentences.zh: 是的，这真的是一项需要亲力亲为的工作。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, they're really fighting on all fronts.
sentences.zh: 对啊，我的意思是，他们真的在各个前线作战。

sentences.en: I mean, just God bless them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，上帝保佑他们。

sentences.en: They've also implemented something across the country called vulture safe zones or V.S.Zs.
sentences.zh: 他们还在全国范围内实施了一项名为“秃鹰安全区”（V.S.Z.）的计划。

sentences.en: So these these V.S.Zs like that areas where there's a hundred kilometer radius area where they really,
sentences.zh: 所以这些 V.S.Z. 就像是一个方圆一百公里的区域，在那里他们真的，

sentences.en: really work hard with the farmers and everybody else to make sure that that area is diclofenac free.
sentences.zh: 真的非常努力地与农民和其他所有人合作，以确保该区域没有双氯芬酸。

sentences.en: They've already started doing some test releases in these areas.
sentences.zh: 他们已经在这些地区开始进行一些测试性放归。

sentences.en: And the idea is that let's start somewhere and maybe one day it'll be safe to fully release these birds.
sentences.zh: 这个想法是，让我们从某个地方开始，也许有一天，完全放归这些鸟类将是安全的。

sentences.en: Yeah, but I mean, the big problem with that is that vultures can fly and I imagine they fly a lot further.
sentences.zh: 是的，但我的意思是，其中最大的问题是秃鹰会飞，而且我想它们会飞得更远。

sentences.en: Than a hundred kilometers.
sentences.zh: 比一百公里远得多。

sentences.en: They can.
sentences.zh: 它们确实能。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so it's it's this interesting thing where the strategy is to create this this zone.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个很有趣的事情，战略是创建这个区域。

sentences.en: But ultimately, it's it's an imaginary zone.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，这是一个想象中的区域。

sentences.en: It's an imaginary line that it's not like the vultures are aware of this.
sentences.zh: 这是一条虚拟的线，并不是说秃鹰自己能意识到这一点。

sentences.en: But Vibhu and others will tell you that at least it's something.
sentences.zh: 但维布和其他人会告诉你，这总比没有强。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I'm glad that they're trying something.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴他们正在尝试做点什么。

sentences.en: And so what's going on with vultures beyond India?
sentences.zh: 那么，印度以外地区的秃鹰情况如何？

sentences.en: Yeah, every country in South Asia is on its own journey and it's slightly different because, you know, the the governments will make different decisions.
sentences.zh: 是的，南亚的每个国家都在经历自己的历程，而且略有不同，因为，你知道，政府会做出不同的决定。

sentences.en: There's a lot of different kind of forces at play that mean that every every country kind of is seeing a different version of this.
sentences.zh: 有许多不同的力量在起作用，这意味着每个国家都在经历不同版本的现状。

sentences.en: An interesting success story, though, is Nepal.
sentences.zh: 不过，一个有趣的成功案例是尼泊尔。

sentences.en: Nepal, it's hard to compare the two countries, Nepal and India, because, you know, India is much larger.
sentences.zh: 尼泊尔，很难将尼泊尔和印度这两个国家进行比较，因为，你知道，印度要大得多。

sentences.en: The catastrophe was also much larger.
sentences.zh: 那场灾难也大得多。

sentences.en: There were more vultures there.
sentences.zh: 那里的秃鹰更多。

sentences.en: But also Diclofenac came on the market in India several years before Nepal.
sentences.zh: 而且双氯芬酸在印度上市的时间比尼泊尔早了好几年。

sentences.en: And so by the time they they found that Diclofenac was the problem, there was just a little bit more time.
sentences.zh: 因此，当他们发现双氯芬酸是问题所在时，他们已经多争取了一点时间。

sentences.en: They had more time before a total collapse happened in Nepal.
sentences.zh: 在尼泊尔发生全面崩溃之前，他们拥有更多的时间。

sentences.en: But Nepal has taken on a really interesting strategy that a lot of people point to as one of the reasons for its success.
sentences.zh: 但尼泊尔采取了一种非常有趣的策略，许多人将其视为成功的原因之一。

sentences.en: Besides vulture safe zones and captive breeding, which they have also in Nepal, they also have a community led effort called Vulture Restaurants.
sentences.zh: 除了他们尼泊尔也有的秃鹰安全区和人工繁育外，他们还有一个由社区主导的项目，叫做“秃鹰餐厅”。

sentences.en: It's not a new concept.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个新概念。

sentences.en: It was borrowed from conservation work in Europe and in Africa.
sentences.zh: 它是从欧洲和非洲的保护工作中借鉴过来的。

sentences.en: But vulture restaurants are essentially areas out in the open in fields, so not in captivity, where the vultures have gotten used to food being provided for them,
sentences.zh: 但秃鹰餐厅本质上是野外开阔地带的区域，也就是非人工圈养区，秃鹰在那里已经习惯了有人给它们提供食物，

sentences.en: specifically drug safe food.
sentences.zh: 特别是对药物安全的食物。

sentences.en: So they so people will go test these drugs and and bring a bunch of food.
sentences.zh: 所以人们会去检测这些药物，然后带上一堆食物。

sentences.en: And it's it's even become kind of a way to boost local economies.
sentences.zh: 这甚至已经成为一种促进当地经济的方式。

sentences.en: It's for it's turned into kind of a tourist attraction where people will come.
sentences.zh: 它变成了一种旅游景点，人们会前来参观。

sentences.en: They'll they'll pay some money to watch these vultures eat.
sentences.zh: 他们会付一些钱来观看这些秃鹰进食。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a thing that vultures have gotten used to.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是秃鹰已经习惯了的事情。

sentences.en: Like, OK, here and here and here are reliable sources of consistent food.
sentences.zh: 比如，好吧，这里、这里和这里是稳定可靠的食物来源。

sentences.en: I'm going to go here instead of needing to look for my own food.
sentences.zh: 我要去这里，而不需要自己去寻找食物。

sentences.en: Yeah, even though it's it's out in the wild.
sentences.zh: 是的，尽管这其实是在野外。

sentences.en: It's it's been effective.
sentences.zh: 但它确实很有效。

sentences.en: And so what do you think the future is going to hold for vultures in India?
sentences.zh: 那么，你认为印度的秃鹰未来会怎样？

sentences.en: I think what's clear is that the population of vultures in India is never going to go back to what it once was, even if the population is stable and healthy.
sentences.zh: 我认为很明显的是，印度的秃鹰种群永远不可能恢复到过去的水平，即使种群数量稳定且健康。

sentences.en: And that's because humans and animals were continuously adapting.
sentences.zh: 这是因为人类和动物一直在不断适应。

sentences.en: And now that the vultures are gone, cities and states in India are grappling with what to do with their dead cows that are just lying open.
sentences.zh: 既然秃鹰已经消失，印度的城市和邦正在努力应对如何处理那些暴露在外的死牛。

sentences.en: And they're trying to to corner them off and put them in these dump sites or in these incinerators.
sentences.zh: 他们正试图把它们围起来，送进这些倾倒场或焚烧炉中。

sentences.en: What that means for vultures, should they return, is that their food supply will be dramatically reduced.
sentences.zh: 对秃鹰来说，如果它们回归，这意味着它们的食物供应将大幅减少。

sentences.en: And in their absence, we're going to we're we need to adapt.
sentences.zh: 在它们缺席的情况下，我们需要去适应。

sentences.en: You know, we need to figure out a new system.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们需要想出一个新的系统。

sentences.en: And so it's this back and forth.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个来回拉锯的过程。

sentences.en: It's this continuous thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一个持续的过程。

sentences.en: When it comes to thinking about the future of vultures in India, I think an image that I just want to leave you with is an image that Vibhu left me with,
sentences.zh: 当考虑印度秃鹰的未来时，我想留给你的一个画面是维布留给我的画面，

sentences.en: which is that in the future, should we see, you know, successful releases of these vultures?
sentences.zh: 那就是在未来，如果我们看到，你知道，这些秃鹰被成功放归，

sentences.en: Even if they all get released, the reality is that they they might not survive in urban areas.
sentences.zh: 即使它们全部被放归，现实是它们可能无法在城市地区生存。

sentences.en: They might not flock to urban areas anymore, like places like Dungravati in Mumbai, for example, because there's so many other things that are in the way.
sentences.zh: 它们可能不再群居在城市地区，比如孟买的东格拉瓦蒂等地，因为有太多其他障碍挡在路上。

sentences.en: You know, these high rise buildings that are blocking their flight path.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些阻挡它们飞行路线的高层建筑。

sentences.en: The country of India is going through this like rapid process of electrification.
sentences.zh: 印度正在经历这样一个快速的电气化进程。

sentences.en: And so all of these wires are in the way of the vultures, you know, and and that may be what the future holds.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些电线都挡住了秃鹰的路，你知道，这可能就是未来的写照。

sentences.en: Is that vultures kind of cordon themselves off to areas that are that are more protected, that are more wild.
sentences.zh: 那就是秃鹰将自己限定在受到更多保护、更加野生的区域。

sentences.en: They stay on the mountains, the cliff sides.
sentences.zh: 它们呆在山脉上、悬崖边。

sentences.en: They stay in the forests.
sentences.zh: 它们呆在森林里。

sentences.en: 30 years ago, vultures could survive in Delhi, but now they cannot.
sentences.zh: 30 年前，秃鹰能在德里生存，但现在它们不能了。

sentences.en: So now ultimately, vultures will be confined to protected areas.
sentences.zh: 所以最终，秃鹰将只限于保护区内。

sentences.en: That is going to happen.
sentences.zh: 这是必然会发生的。

sentences.en: I asked Vibhu how the prospect of this made him feel.
sentences.zh: 我问维布对此有什么感受。

sentences.en: You know, in his childhood, he was so used to seeing vultures just everywhere.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在他的童年里，他太习惯于到处看到秃鹰了。

sentences.en: So many people were.
sentences.zh: 很多人都是如此。

sentences.en: But what if vultures never returned to these places?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果秃鹰再也不会回到这些地方呢？

sentences.en: I think that will be good.
sentences.zh: 我想那会是件好事。

sentences.en: They had done a good service for us when we didn't have the resources.
sentences.zh: 当我们没有资源的时候，它们为我们服务得很好。

sentences.en: Now we have to take care of the cattle ourselves.
sentences.zh: 现在我们必须自己照顾牛只了。

sentences.en: Yeah, we've proven ourselves to be not very good neighbors.
sentences.zh: 是的，事实证明我们并不是很好的邻居。

sentences.en: So for their own sake, maybe they should just stay away for their own good.
sentences.zh: 所以为了它们自己的好，为了它们自身的安全，也许它们还是远离为妙。

sentences.en: This is really fascinating, Lasha.
sentences.zh: 这真的太迷人了，拉莎。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for this like extra time and just the beautiful story that you produced and all this extra information.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你抽出额外的时间，以及你制作的精彩故事和所有这些额外的信息。

sentences.en: I love this stuff.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢这些内容了。

sentences.en: It makes me so happy to learn.
sentences.zh: 能学到这些让我感到非常高兴。

sentences.en: And I appreciate you taking the time to talk to me about it.
sentences.zh: 我很感激你花时间和我谈论这件事。

sentences.en: Thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: This was really fun.
sentences.zh: 这真的很有趣。
